Hi Grace,

Thanks for the quick standup yesterday. Our payments team saw tokenization failures between 09:02 and 09:44 PT on 29 Mar; this caused a visible queueing effect in our customer gateway and about ~0.6% of requests to return 5xx.

We need a consolidated closure packet we can share with our internal risk and ops teams: an executive summary, a timeline with timestamps (UTC and PT), the root cause hypothesis, concrete mitigations you are implementing, and any evidence artifacts we can verify (logs / S3 paths / Drive link).

Can you also include a short checklist our engineering lead can run to validate the fix (what to query, which logs to look for)? We want to verify before we sign off.

Elena

Subject: March 30 outage — verification brief and action ledger

Elena — thanks for the details and for flagging the acceptance checklist requirement. Attaching the pack we promised: a short executive summary, a minute-by-minute timeline (CSV), an evidence bundle (logs + sanitized traces), and an action ledger with owners and deadlines. Attachments (stubs): [Attachment: outage-timeline.csv (text/csv)], [Attachment: evidence-bundle.zip (application/zip)], [Attachment: postincident-action-ledger.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)].

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Incident window: 2027-03-29T16:02:00Z — 2027-03-29T16:44:00Z (09:02 — 09:44 PT).
- Impact: transient increased 5xx errors affecting tokenization service; peak error rate ~0.6% for matched traffic patterns; no customer data exfiltration.
- Root cause (short): a latency regression in KV cache eviction logic triggered by a rare sequence-length distribution spike combined with a mis-graded kernel selection path on a recently deployed optimization.

What we included in the packet:
1) outage-timeline.csv — minute-level events, request ids, token-latency percentiles.
2) evidence-bundle.zip — sanitized request traces (redacted user ids), scheduler logs, and a QuickTrace run for a failing request id.
3) postincident-action-ledger.xlsx — owners, targeted delivery dates, verification steps.

Immediate mitigations already applied (completed within 45 minutes):
- Rolled back the kernel-selection heuristic for the affected model family (owner: david_kim).
- Reapplied a conservative KV cache threshold to disable aggressive eviction while we collect telemetry (owner: ben_carter).
- Applied an emergency routing rule to route sensitive production traffic to the dedicated pool for higher isolation (owner: infra-ops).

Planned follow-ups (from ledger):
- Deep kernel regression test and new unit test coverage (due 2027-04-06) — david_kim
- Quantization/heuristic guardrail: autoscaling flags and canary gating to prevent future regressions (due 2027-04-13) — ben_carter
- Evidence verification walkthrough (see checklist below) — grace_oconnor

Quick verification checklist for MapleBank engineers (copy to your ops runbook):
- Confirm the gateway 5xx rate has returned to baseline for 2027-03-29 10:00–12:00 PT. Query: requests.metrics.errors{service:tokenizer,env:prod} / minute.
- Check the attached outage-timeline.csv for any remaining request ids with error > 500 around 16:02–16:44 UTC.
- Download the QuickTrace from evidence-bundle.zip and confirm KV cache miss counts are back to expected levels for the same request ids.
- Validate that traffic to the dedicated pool shows no elevated latencies (see sequence latency p50/p95 in the CSV).

Next steps: we propose a 30-min verification call Thursday 2027-04-01 10:00 PT to walk through the checklist together. I also created a shared Drive folder with the artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2BMapleBankEvidence.

If this looks good I will mark the ledger state as "awaiting customer verification" and update the hubspot deal record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/MapleBank/DB-15937.

Thanks — and really appreciate the quick coordination.

Best,

Grace / Ben — quick technical note to include in the ledger and evidence bundle for Elena's team. Adding here so it's in-thread.

1) Cause detail (long form): the rollback we performed reverted a new kernel-selection heuristic that aimed to pick quantized kernels under short-sequence conditions. During a burst of mixed short+long sequences the heuristic mis-classified several batches, which forced a fall-back path that increased KV cache churn. That churn caused a cascade of latency amplification for tokenization requests where KV lookups were on the hot path.

2) Why it was rare: the sequence-length distribution that triggers the mis-classification is <0.2% of global traffic and surfaced only under a specific traffic footprint that MapleBank's gateway produces (many small bursts with occasional long sequences).

3) Evidence pointers to include in the packet (explicit):
- scheduler.log lines with tag KERNEL_SELECT id=<request id> (search for markers in evidence-bundle/logs/).
- QuickTrace for a failing request id (QT-req-44922) included in the zip.
- KV metric series: kv.cache.evictions and kv.cache.miss_rate for the timeframe (CSV column names in outage-timeline.csv).

4) Temporary guard: I recommend adding a lightweight canary gate that measures sequence-length percentiles and disables the new heuristic above the 99.5th percentile until we ship the regression test.

I put provisional owners and due dates in the ledger (postincident-action-ledger.xlsx). Happy to join the verification call on Thursday.

—David
David Kim
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
